text:
sara (product): Heads-up — inbound from Acme: they want reserved capacity discounts, the ability to apply prepaid credits across multiple projects, and a hard overage cap. Need guidance on what we can promise and what needs engineering/legal. Can product weigh in?

miguel (sales): They asked for a sample sheet: committed monthly tokens -> price, rollover of unused credits, and an overage cap at no more than 150% of committed spend. They want numbers for a PO by Friday.

kevin (support): Filed ticket S-9821 with customer usage profile and ask. Attaching their 3-month token histogram. Quick note: they already hit burst limits twice this quarter.

olga (finance): High level constraints: credits are accounting liabilities — rollover increases recognition complexity. Short-term we can do 12-month expiry rolling forward; multi-project pooling is fine if we treat it as a single contract. Need legal sign-off for cap/credits language.

jen (eng): Engineering implications: billing has current support for per-customer credits and basic overage charging. Rollover + project pooling requires adding a shared-balance layer and console UI + metering changes. MVP path: allow manual pooling on our side (sales ops) + automated pooling in next quarter.

miguel (sales): Manual pooling is fine as a short-term promise if product commits to a roadmap item. Customer prefers automated pooling but will accept manual for initial term.

olga (finance): Also recommend limiting rollover window to 12 months and disallow retroactive credits. That keeps revenue recognition tractable.

jen (eng): For overage cap we can implement a billing rule: cap overage to X% of committed spend and route excess to account manager approval before auto-billing. That avoids huge surprise debits. Implementation estimate: 2 sprints for backend + 1 sprint for console changes.

kevin (support): From support ops: if we allow manual pooling, we need a clear playbook for when customers hit burst beyond capacity: emails, temporary bursts allowed, then billing review. Can we standardize that?

sara (product): Proposed product decision (draft): 1) Offer three simple SKU tiers for reserved capacity (S, M, L) with fixed monthly committed token volumes and discounted per-token rates. 2) Allow credits to be pooled across projects for enterprise contracts but mark as "manual pooling" until automated pooling ships. 3) Credits expire after 12 months. 4) Overages billed at 125% of committed per-token rate by default; customer can request a one-time cap review that requires approval. 5) Public pricing remains unchanged. Internal deal-specific adjustments go through sales ops.

miguel (sales): That sounds workable. Can we get concrete numbers? Even rough placeholders are fine for the PO. Suggest discounts roughly: S=10% off hosted, M=20% off, L=30% off. Also a one-time onboarding credit for first month?

olga (finance): Rough numbers OK for sales, but contracts must include explicit terms on expiry and non-transferability unless we do pooling. Onboarding credits must be expensed upfront; prefer those be limited and visible.

jen (eng): For the sample sheet, I can provide a config example for our billing system:

```
reserved_tier: large
committed_tokens: 2_000_000_000
per_token_rate_committed: $0.00007
overage_rate: per_token_rate_committed * 1.25
rollover_window_months: 12
pooling: manual
```

sara (product): Launch criteria for enabling this for a single customer (MVP):
- legal signs off on pooled credits & expiry language
- finance approves sample pricing and accounting treatment
- sales ops can manage manual pooling via internal process
- engineering implements overage billing rules and a simple billing note in console
Once MVP is live, automated pooling and console UX will be roadmap items for the next quarter.

miguel (sales): Action items for me: get customer to confirm committed tier by EOD Thursday, request PO with their preferred pooling scope.

kevin (support): I'll draft the playbook for burst incidents and escalate matrix.

jen (eng): I'll scope backend work and flag any blockers. Estimate ETA if approved: 4 weeks for MVP.

olga (finance): I'll draft the accounting note and sample term language for legal.

billing-bot: New ticket created: BILL-4473 (reserved-pricing-mvp) assigned to billing-team.

sara (product): Ok — product decision: ship MVP with manual pooling and a 12-month expiry, overage at 125% by default, discount tiers S/M/L as suggested. Approval contingent on legal & finance sign-off. If anyone objects, call it out now.

miguel (sales): No objections from me. I'll push for the onboarding credit but acceptable if finance vetoes.

olga (finance): No further objections; will push back on any open-ended credits.

jen (eng): Good with MVP scope. Will start the ticketing work.

sara (product): Great — I'll summarize and put this into the backlog as product:reserved-pricing-mvp and include launch criteria + owners. Thanks all.
